subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency (Finly)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Verma <samir@finly.com>, Elena Park <elena@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency (Finly)

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, current state, and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please reply with corrections / clarifications.

Attendees: Samir (Finly), Elena (Finly), Marissa (Redwood), Aditya (Redwood)

Top pain points (as described)
- p95 latency is inconsistent (~1.0–1.4s today) and spikes during batch/peak windows
- Streaming UX is unreliable: initial token delay + intermittent stutter under concurrency
- Memory pressure/evictions on KV cache causing tail latency and dropped tokens

Current stack (high level) — Pallet from the call
- Inference: mix of managed provider + on-prem VLLM (4x A100), nginx LB
- Cache: Redis for prefix/KV cache
- Orchestration: home-grown autoscaler, traffic routed via API gateway

Quantified performance targets (requested)
- Short-term p95 target (non-streaming generation): <= 300ms (goal: <= 250ms)
- Streaming UX: initial token displayed <= 150ms; no perceptible stutter up to baseline concurrency
- Concurrency: baseline 300–400 concurrent streaming sessions; spikes to ~800–900 for quarter-end jobs

Success criteria for PoC
1) End-to-end p95 (client->server->first-token) consistently <= 300ms for targeted traffic profile
2) Smooth streaming at baseline concurrency (no stutter, <5% packetized delays)
3) No model-level token drops during 95th percentile load; memory pressure handled gracefully

Next steps (proposed)
- Finly: share 48hrs of representative traffic logs / curl traces + a couple sample payloads (size, sequence length)
- Redwood: run a short baseline performance plan and provide a PoC deck + estimated cost for Dedicated pool
- Schedule technical deep-dive with Finly infra + Redwood serving team (target: Wed, Jul 07)
- Procurement: loop in Finly procurement contact so we can share pricing/contract timing

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (application/pdf)]

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive once you confirm availability.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
[redwood.com]

From: Samir Verma <samir@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@finly.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency (Finly)

Thanks Marissa — this matches what we discussed. A few clarifications / added context:

- Current numbers: our observed p95 for small interactive queries (avg ~50 tokens) is ~1.2s, for larger batch jobs it hits 1.8–2.5s depending on concurrency.
- Streaming problems: initial latency varies widely (200–800ms) and when we hit concurrency spikes we see bursts of stutter where the stream pauses for multiple hundred ms before resuming. This particularly impacts the collaborative editor UX.
- Infra: we run 4x A100 nodes for on-prem inference with an nginx front end and Redis for prefix cache. We also use a managed provider for overflow traffic.

We can share logs and sample traces (I’ll put together a small S3 bucket link). Procurement contact is procurement@finly.com (cc’ed here as requested).

We’re highly interested in a Dedicated PoC — curious if Redwood can meet a 300ms p95 target for interactive traffic, and what the expected concurrency headroom is. Also important: SOC 2 compliance for production data and the ability to support EU residency later this year.

Available for a technical deep-dive on Jul 7 between 9–12 PT.

—
Samir Verma
Head of Product Engineering | Finly
samir@finly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Verma <samir@finly.com>, Elena Park <elena@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency (Finly)

Appreciate the detail, Samir — that helps. Two quick follow-ups before the deep-dive:

1) Can you attach a sample of the typical request payloads (prompt length distribution, avg tokens returned) and a 48-hour trace (curl or client-side) so we can model realistic arrival rates?
2) Can you confirm whether the spikes are predictable (scheduled batch jobs/end-of-day jobs) or user-driven (organic traffic)? You mentioned quarter-end jobs — are those daily/hourly?

On our side we’ll put together a short benchmarking plan for the PoC. Key benchmarking knobs we’ll explore:
- Dedicated pool sizing and autoscaling behavior under streaming load
- Continuous prefix/KV caching effectiveness for repeated prompts
- Batch sizing, tokenization overhead, and quantization tradeoffs for throughput vs. latency

I’m attaching a short telemetry checklist that lists the logs and traces that will be most valuable. If you can drop those in the Drive link below prior to the deep-dive, we’ll run a quick baseline simulation.

Attachments: [Attachment: telemetry-checklist.csv (text/csv)]
Related link: https://drive.google.com/finly-sample-logs

I’ll send a calendar invite for Jul 7, 10:00 PT unless you prefer a different time.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena@finly.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Samir Verma <samir@finly.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency (Finly)

Adding a few procurement/security clarifications from our side:
- Procurement: we’re interested in committed capacity pricing for Dedicated for predictable cost during peak months — procurement@finly.com will own contract discussions.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is a hard requirement for production; EU data residency is a future requirement but not immediate for this PoC.
- Concurrency details: baseline ~350 concurrent streaming sessions, spikes up to ~900 once a month (quarter-end), and occasional hourly spikes to ~600.
- Target detail: initial token <= 150ms if possible; overall p95 <= 300ms for interactive workloads.

We’ll share the traces and a short traffic calendar so you can replicate the spike patterns. Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—
Elena Park
VP, Engineering | Finly
elena@finly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-05T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Finly PoC ask & next steps

Quick internal summary and asks after Finly thread:

Summary:
- Finly baseline: ~350 concurrent streaming sessions, spikes to ~900 (monthly). Current p95 ~1.2s; target p95 <=300ms (goal 250ms).
- Streaming UX priority: initial token <=150ms and no stutter at baseline concurrency.

Immediate action items:
- Aditya: can you run an internal simulation using our streaming stack to estimate a Dedicated pool size that supports 400 steady concurrent streams + headroom to 1k? Include KV cache sizing and Redis footprint estimate.
- Mateo: draft a short PoC plan (server topology, telemetry requirements, SLAs we can reasonably offer for the PoC) and a rough month-on-month cost estimate for Dedicated capacity.
- Marissa: I’ll own scheduling the deep-dive on Jul 7 and collecting Finly traces once they upload. I’ll also pull together the benchmarking checklist and sample scripts.

Priority: high — Finly indicated procurement interest and wants pricing/PoC details quickly.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
